items.review_rationale: Read unital left module action over an associative ring with identity, on additive abelian group, distinguishing order of left multiplication and scalar identity requirement.

references.phrase: left scalar action R x M to M
references.context: Action taking scalar first and additive-group element second, with output in M.
Scalar multiplication distributes over addition in M.
Additivity in the ring scalar argument.
Left action preserves left-to-right algebra multiplication composition.
Specified multiplicative identity of R acts as identity on all m in M.

items.review_rationale: Read unital right module as abelian additive group with scalar action on right respecting distributivity and associativity plus m1=m, without swapping it to left-module action.

references.phrase: right scalar action M x R to M
references.context: Scalar multiplication with module element first and scalar second.
Action distributes over addition in both module and ring.
Action order agrees with right-sided multiplication by successive scalars.
The specified ring identity acts trivially on the right of each module element.

references.disposition: Right action is not silently identified with a left action over a noncommutative ring.

items.review_rationale: Read congruence of integers modulo a strictly positive integer as divisibility of the difference by m, requiring integer witness k and fixed modulus.

references.context: Integer m strictly greater than zero, fixed when comparing residues.

references.phrase: integer divisibility of a-b by m
references.context: There exists integer k such that the integer difference a-b equals k*m.

references.phrase: congruence relation a equivalent b modulo m
references.context: Binary equivalence relation determined by the positive modulus m.

references.disposition: The sourced convention restricts m to positive integers; no negative or zero modulus equivalence introduced.

items.review_rationale: Read least-nonnegative-remainder characterization of integer congruence for positive modulus, separating Euclidean division from equivalence of the resulting residues.

references.context: Integer m greater than zero with respect to usual order on Z.

references.phrase: least nonnegative remainder upon division by m
references.context: Unique integer r in {0,...,m-1} such that a=q*m+r for some integer q.
Remainder computed for a and b at the same fixed positive modulus m is identical.

references.disposition: Same integer-congruence meaning as divisibility-of-difference definition; a self-link is not a mathematical prerequisite.
